kumar.s: quick summary of the per-layer outlier scan i ran on redwood-7b-v2-int8 run yesterday. produced a compact sensitivity ranking and a conservative mitigation plan. paste below and looking for engineering + eval thumbs/comments.

kumar.s: results — from 512 eval prompts (mix of summarization + qa):
- baseline FP16 MMLU-like proxy acc: 72.1%
- straight INT8 (awq per-tensor with standard calibration) acc: 67.4% (delta -4.7)
- straight GPTQ (8-bit with per-channel quant) acc: 71.0% (delta -1.1)
- FP8 experimental (a toy run) acc: 69.5% (delta -2.6)

kumar.s: per-layer sensitivity (top-5 worst layers by KL/ppl contrib):
1) transformer.layers.22.ffn.w2 (huge channel outliers)
2) transformer.layers.16.attn.q_proj (skewed activations at long prompts)
3) transformer.layers.9.ffn.w1
4) transformer.layers.33.attn.o_proj
5) transformer.layers.2.embeddings

kumar.s: short analysis — the biggest regressions are dominated by a handful of FFN dense matrices that have very heavy-tailed channel activations. per-channel dynamic range is ~10-20x larger in those channels vs median. AWQ/int8 baseline clips those which kills accuracy. GPTQ per-channel helps but still suffers unless we rescue the worst 2-3 layers.

maya: nice work. curious about the cutoff heuristic you used to mark a layer as "outlier"?

kumar.s: i used a combined score: 0.5 * normalized KL divergence (quantized vs fp16 intermediate activations) + 0.3 * max_channel_ratio (max_abs_channel / median_abs_channel) + 0.2 * delta-ppl when quantizing layer in isolation. threshold tuned to flag ~3-6 layers for this model.

simon: can you paste the per-layer isolated-quant table? even a tiny snippet is fine.

kumar.s: pasted sample:
```
layer, kl_norm, max_ch_ratio, isolated_delta_ppl
layers.22.ffn.w2, 0.72, 18.4, 3.9
layers.16.attn.q, 0.48, 6.2, 1.6
layers.9.ffn.w1, 0.41, 5.1, 1.2
layers.33.attn.o, 0.39, 4.8, 0.9
layers.2.emb, 0.35, 3.1, 0.6
```

eileen: proposal idea — hybrid profile: AWQ default + GPTQ for flagged layers + run-time "layer-skip" to fall back to FP16 for top-1 layer under pressure. thoughts?

kumar.s: exactly. my proposed bakeoff plan:
- profile run: identify top-N outlier layers via above score (N default 3)
- build hybrid artifact: AWQ for all layers except top-N -> use GPTQ quantization on those top-N with per-channel scales
- add a token-accurate runtime guard: if latency SLO > X or memory contention, instead of degrading whole model, dynamically mark the single worst layer to run in FP16 (fast-path memory checkout).
- add evaluation: calibrate hybrid on 2k holdout prompts and measure MMLU-proxy, avg token perplexity, and social-output tests.

zach: the runtime guard worries me — switching a single layer to FP16 could blow memory for larger sizes. did you measure memory delta?

kumar.s: yes — for 7b model the incremental peak memory for one layer FP16 vs quant is ~0.9 GB in our runtime with KV caching. on 13B it's ~2.2 GB. so the guard only makes sense for dedicated instances with headroom. we can gate by deployment profile.

maya: eval-bench numbers on hybrid?

kumar.s: hybrid (AWQ everywhere + GPTQ on top-3) acc: 71.8% (delta -0.3 vs FP16). latency uplift: +6% median token time. cost per-token ~ +4% vs straight AWQ.

eval-bot: CI run results summary attached (sanity):
- hybrid: pass accuracy_regressions (tolerance 1.0%)
- straight-int8: fail (delta 4.7%)
- gptq-all: pass but higher memory + slower batching

simon: nice. actionable followups?

kumar.s: action list: 
1) eng-runtime: add a runtime flag to mark layer ranges to run in FP16 and a fallback trigger based on memory guard (ops-bot tagged)
2) eng-ml: automate per-layer sensitivity scan in the onboarding pipeline and emit hybrid-quant profiles as artifacts
3) eval: expand the calibration set to 10k prompts and run golden metrics across multiple workloads (chat, summarization, code)
4) infra: add a dedicated-small instance flavor with +2GB headroom for hybrid-fallback testing

ops-bot: created ticket INF-3821 to add per-layer-flag support to runtime (link: https://tickets.internal/INF-3821) :white_check_mark:

eileen: small nit — we should also try clipping vs scaling per-channel. AWQ clip tends to bias downward. maybe try h-scaling where we apply a per-channel multiplier to compress dynamic range before quant. could reduce KL without full GPTQ.

kumar.s: agreed. part of the bakeoff matrix: AWQ, AWQ+channel-clip, AWQ+h-scale, GPTQ-topN, FP16-top1. test matrix combinatorics small (5x).

zach: timeline?

kumar.s: plan to run automated bakeoffs over the week. eng-runtime ticket PR due EOW, eng-ml pipeline change PR mid-next-week, eval runs complete by next Friday.

eileen: :thumbsup:

maya: thanks — this looks ready to spin up. can you drop the raw per-channel histograms somewhere?

kumar.s: uploaded to s3://redwood-experiments/hybrid-quant/1772500000/hists.tar.gz and added pointer to the ticket.

simon: one more ask — add a small nonparametric test: measure top-5 token rank stability for important prompts pre/post quant. that catches cases where ppl looks fine but top1 changes.

kumar.s: good idea — will add top-k rank-stability. will post updated results to the ticket when runs finish.
